name: paper-derived-models
title: Paper-derived mechanistic models
lead:
Two studies mine the "Articles of interest - BV" reading list for runnable
models. Each turns a published quantitative mechanism into a viva-tellurium ODE
composite, runs it, and checks the source paper's headline against graded
acceptance criteria. Together they show the composition layer can absorb
literature mechanisms — one newly assembled, one a faithful recreation of a
published model on a curated BioModels base.

at_a_glance.role: BV biogenic-amine cross-feeding — bistable community/pH ODE (newly assembled from Borgogna/Puebla kinetics).
Kim 2021 one-carbon / menstrual-cycle recreation — estradiol->CBS->homocysteine on the curated Reed2004 SBML.

biological_story:
The bacterial-vaginosis and women's-health literature describes two mechanisms
that are quantitative enough to model directly. First, biogenic amines are not
just a BV marker: Gardnerella-associated amines inhibit Lactobacillus growth and
suppress its lactic-acid production, raising vaginal pH, while Lactobacillus in
turn degrades those amines and grows faster at low pH. Closing that loop produces
a bistable community — a protective, acidic, Lactobacillus-dominant state in which
amines are cleared, and a BV state in which Gardnerella sustains a ~millimolar
amine pool at higher pH. This reframes biogenic amines as a bistability-generating
mechanism and therefore a therapeutic target (an amine-degrading probiotic shifts
the basin boundary).

Second, the same hormone that shapes the vaginal environment — estradiol — also
controls one-carbon metabolism in the liver. Kim, Nijhout and Reed showed that
estradiol activates cystathionine-beta-synthase (CBS), the transsulfuration enzyme
that clears homocysteine, so hepatic homocysteine falls as estradiol rises across
the menstrual cycle, reaching its minimum near ovulation. Standing that single
estradiol target on the curated Reed2004 methionine cycle reproduces the inverse
relationship, while the methionine cycle re-balances to keep the SAM/SAH
methylation ratio stable. The two studies share a theme central to MOSAIC: sex
hormones couple to metabolism, in the microbiome and in the host alike.
question:
Can mechanistic models recreated from the women's-health / bacterial-vaginosis
literature reproduce their source papers' quantitative claims inside the MOSAIC
process-bigraph composition framework?
hypothesis:
Quantitative mechanisms reported in the reading list — a biogenic-amine
cross-feeding loop (Borgogna 2021, Puebla-Barragan 2021) and estradiol control
of one-carbon metabolism (Kim, Nijhout & Reed 2021) — can each be wrapped as a
runnable composite and reproduce the paper's headline behaviour (bistable
healthy/BV states; homocysteine varying inversely with estradiol over the cycle).

executive.what_is_this:
Two literature-derived mechanistic model studies grouped as one campaign: a BV
biogenic-amine cross-feeding ODE and a recreation of the Kim 2021 one-carbon /
menstrual-cycle model.
executive.verdict:
Both studies reproduce their source paper's headline behaviour. The amine
cross-feeding loop is bistable (protective acidic Lactobacillus state vs a BV
state with a ~mM amine pool); the one-carbon model reproduces the inverse
estradiol-homocysteine relationship over the cycle (corr ~ -0.94).
executive.verdict_detail:
The amine study is a mechanistic-plausibility result (one illustrative
parameterisation, amine-inhibition term anchored to Borgogna 2021); the
one-carbon study is a faithful recreation of Kim 2021 Fig 2 on the curated
Reed2004 methionine-cycle SBML plus Kim's h(E2) CBS forcing.
Automated acceptance gate is PENDING: the member studies' behavior_tests cannot auto-grade on the xarray emitter (a viva_emitters RunReader resolution bug, reported to the discovery-engine session and being fixed). The reproductions themselves are supported by direct-simulation evidence recorded in each study's findings; the gate will compute PASS once the RunReader fix lands.

decisions_needed.question: Calibrate the amine cross-feeding model to a clinical vaginal time series (e.g. Song 2020, PRJNA637322) to map the bistability boundary quantitatively?
decisions_needed.context: The bistability is demonstrated under one illustrative parameterisation but not fitted to data.

decisions_needed.question: Extend the one-carbon recreation to the full Kim 2021 19-ODE network (add the folate cycle + PEMT g(E2) / TS-DHFR u(E2) effects) for a higher-fidelity port?
decisions_needed.context: The current study recreates the methionine-cycle core with folate pools clamped.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
Published quantitative mechanisms from the women's-health literature can be
reproduced as runnable composites that recover the source papers' headline
behaviour.
evidence_for: mosaic_amine_crossfeeding: a biogenic-amine cross-feeding ODE is bistable, reproducing the two-way loop Borgogna 2021 and Puebla-Barragan 2021 quantify (amine growth-inhibition anchored to Borgogna's measured effect size).

mosaic_onecarbon_cycle: estradiol activation of CBS makes homocysteine vary inversely with estradiol over the menstrual cycle (corr ~ -0.94), a faithful recreation of Kim 2021 Fig 2 on the curated Reed2004 methionine-cycle SBML.
key_figures: amine_crossfeeding: Lactobacillus/Gardnerella/amine-pool/pH trajectories resolving to the protective basin.
onecarbon_homocysteine: homocysteine vs estradiol over the 28-day cycle (inverse, minimum at the ovulatory E2 peak).
caveats: The amine study uses one illustrative community/pH parameterisation (not a clinical fit); the bistability is demonstrated, not mapped as a calibrated phase boundary.
The one-carbon study recreates the methionine-cycle core only; Kim's folate-cycle estradiol effects are out of scope of this port.

studies.name: mosaic_amine_crossfeeding
studies.title: BV biogenic-amine cross-feeding

findings.statement: The biogenic-amine cross-feeding ODE is bistable — a protective acidic Lactobacillus attractor and a Gardnerella-dominant BV attractor with a ~mM amine pool — reproducing the two-way loop Borgogna 2021 and Puebla-Barragan 2021 quantify.

evidence.observed: protective basin: Lactobacillus → ~0.94, Gardnerella → ~0.09, amines cleared to ~0.1 mM, pH → 4.3; dysbiotic start instead locks into G-dominant, ~5.4 mM amines, pH 5.8

expected.summary: Borgogna 2021 + Puebla-Barragan 2021 imply a two-way amine loop that should admit both a protective and a BV steady state.

findings.explanation: Amines inhibit Lactobacillus growth and suppress lactate (raising pH, favouring Gardnerella); Lactobacillus degrades amines and acidifies (lowering pH, favouring itself). The opposing feedbacks create two basins of attraction.

findings.statement: In the protective basin Lactobacillus clears the biogenic-amine pool and acidifies the community, closing the amine-degradation arm of the loop.

evidence.observed: amine pool falls from 2000 µM toward ~0.1 mM as Lactobacillus takes over; lactate proxy rises to ~1.6 (pH ~4.3)

expected.summary: Puebla-Barragan 2021 — Lactobacillus crispatus strains degrade putrescine/cadaverine and grow faster at low pH.

studies.claim: A biogenic-amine cross-feeding loop (Gardnerella amines inhibit Lactobacillus and suppress lactate; Lactobacillus degrades amines and acidifies) makes the vaginal community bistable — a protective acidic Lactobacillus state versus a Gardnerella-dominant BV state with a ~mM amine pool.

derived.insight: The biogenic-amine cross-feeding ODE is bistable — a protective acidic Lactobacillus attractor and a Gardnerella-dominant BV attractor with a ~mM amine pool — reproducing the two-way loop Borgogna 2021 and Puebla-Barragan 2021 quantify.

studies.name: mosaic_onecarbon_cycle
studies.title: Kim 2021 one-carbon cycle

findings.statement: Hepatic homocysteine varies inversely with estradiol over the menstrual cycle — minimum at the ovulatory E2 peak, maximum at menstruation — reproducing the central result of Kim, Nijhout & Reed 2021.

evidence.observed: corr(E2, Hcy) ≈ -0.94 over the settled cycle; Hcy ≈ 0.60 µM at the day-12 E2 peak vs ≈ 1.03 µM at menstruation (mean 0.72 µM)

expected.summary: Kim 2021 Fig 2 — homocysteine moves opposite to estradiol across the cycle (lowest near ovulation).

findings.explanation: Estradiol activates CBS via h(E2) = 1 + (E2-0.09)/(0.67+(E2-0.09)); higher CBS flux at the E2 peak consumes more homocysteine through transsulfuration, so Hcy falls as E2 rises.

findings.statement: The inverse relationship is driven by estradiol activation of CBS alone — standing Kim's h(E2) forcing on the curated Reed2004 methionine cycle is sufficient to reproduce it.

evidence.observed: with h(E2) on CBS only (no other estradiol targets), Hcy tracks E2 at corr -0.94; the SAM/SAH methylation ratio stays near-flat (methylation homeostasis, Kim 2021 Fig 3A)

expected.summary: Kim 2021 identifies CBS as the dominant estradiol-sensitive node for the homocysteine response.

studies.claim: Estradiol activation of CBS (transsulfuration) makes hepatic homocysteine vary inversely with estradiol over the menstrual cycle — lowest at the ovulatory E2 peak — reproducing Kim, Nijhout & Reed 2021 on the curated Reed2004 methionine-cycle model.

derived.insight: Hepatic homocysteine varies inversely with estradiol over the menstrual cycle — minimum at the ovulatory E2 peak, maximum at menstruation — reproducing the central result of Kim, Nijhout & Reed 2021.
